claims: The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission started a 10-day crewed journey around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission has four astronauts.
The four astronauts are testing the Orion spacecraft's systems before returning to Earth.
The Artemis II mission includes a high Earth orbit check-out.
The Artemis II mission includes a translunar injection burn.
The Artemis II mission includes a lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission includes a final Pacific Ocean splashdown.
Artemis II lifted off from Kennedy Space Center Complex 39B at 6:24 p.m. EDT on April 1.
On Day 1-2, Orion performs a high Earth orbit check-out of systems.
On Day 1-2, Orion performs manual flying (proximity operations).
On Day 2, the ICPS fires to send Orion on a trajectory to the Moon.
ICPS stands for Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage.
On Day 3-5, travel to the Moon occurs, performing trajectory corrections.
The lunar far side flyby is expected on Day 4.
On Day 6-9, return trajectory towards Earth.
On Day 10, Orion re-enters Earth's atmosphere.
On Day 10, Orion utilizes its heat shield to land safely in the Pacific Ocean.
Reid Wiseman (NASA) is an Artemis II astronaut.
Victor Glover (NASA) is an Artemis II astronaut.
Christina Koch (NASA) is an Artemis II astronaut.
Jeremy Hansen (CSA/Canada) is an Artemis II astronaut.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
